# Monitorability certificate — T11

**Generated by `scripts/73_monitorability_certificate.py` — do not edit by hand.**

Detector `decoder_guard`, judged against a budget of **0.1 false alarms per hour**. The verdict is conditional on that budget and is not meaningful without it.

## Verdict

## NOT MONITORABLE at 0.1 false alarms/hour

## How much independent evidence is in one session?

- Windows per session at non-overlapping spacing: **10**
- Lag-1 autocorrelation: **0.085** (95% CI -0.122 to 0.453)
- Effective independent samples: **8.44**
- Episodes measured: 17
- Source: fault-free episodes (scripts/70)

**The estimator's ceiling at 10 windows is 0.59.** Feed it a series whose true correlation is 0.999 and that is what it reports, so any measured value near the ceiling is a limit of the measurement rather than a property of the signal. This is stated here because it is easy to misread and because this project misread it once.

## What a warning costs

| Quantity | Value |
|---|---|
| Median lead time | **-20.0 s** |
| Lead time 95% CI | -25.0 s to -10.0 s |
| False alarms per hour | **3.4069** |
| Within the 0.1/hour budget | **no** |
| Faults detected | 143/586 |
| Warning threshold used | 50.457864979261146 |

Lead time and false-alarm rate are reported together, always. Either can be made to look excellent by sacrificing the other, so a single figure is not interpretable. The threshold that produced this pair was chosen on the validation split and applied unchanged to the test split.

## Gates

**2 of 5 passed.** They are applied in order and a detector that fails the first is not carried forward: a monitor that alarms during healthy operation is disqualified however well it detects faults.

| Gate | Result |
|---|---|
| Silence — quiet when nothing is wrong | **FAIL** |
| Rate invariance — not just total activity | **FAIL** |
| Comparator — beats counting spikes | pass |
| Elapsed time — not just tracking the clock | **FAIL** |
| Detrend — silence survives removing a linear trend | pass |

## Reading this honestly

**Not monitorable at this budget because 3 of five gates failed; the warning does not arrive before the failure; the false-alarm rate exceeds the budget.**

This is a measurement, not a defeat. It says what this array's monitoring costs, in numbers somebody else can check and compare against their own hardware. Nobody could state that before, because in observational recordings the onset of degradation is never written down, so lead time depends on the analyst's definition and the false-alarm rate is not estimable at all.

**What this certificate cannot tell you:** whether a different detector would do better, whether a longer session would help, or whether the result transfers to a different array. Those are separate measurements, and this instrument is built to make each of them runnable.
